thesis: This is the clearest do-not-chase in the book. CSL is A$169.50 after a 62.7% three-month run, which puts it roughly 20% above the A$139.20 average analyst target, and the run is a relief rally off a guidance reset rather than a growth surprise: FY26 underlying earnings fell 2% with US$7.1B of impairments driving a statutory loss, and FY27 guidance is flat revenue with about 5% underlying profit growth. Even the packet says the trend is incomplete - above SMA200 but SMA50 not aligned.
bull_case: The re-rating has real content behind it. CSL jumped 17.25% on 18 August on results that beat a reset guidance bar, then added 5.49% the next day to A$166.48. Three things changed the narrative: underlying earnings ahead of guidance, greater clarity on US pharmaceutical pricing arrangements, and a substantial manufacturing expansion in Illinois. The transformation programme delivered about US$176M of savings, beating its initial target, and that is what underpins the ~5% FY27 profit growth guide. Momentum is extraordinary at +62.7% over 63 days, and one broker sees another 40% of upside. Price is above SMA200.
bear_case: Buying 20% above the average analyst target after a 62.7% run is paying for the re-rating twice. The underlying business did not grow - FY26 underlying earnings *fell* 2%, and US$7.1B of impairments produced a statutory loss; FY27 guidance is flat revenue and about 5% profit growth, which does not support a 62.7% quarter on any normal multiple. The move is a sentiment repair off a May guidance reset, and repairs finish. Structure agrees the trend is not clean: the packet flags 'above SMA200 but SMA50 not aligned' - it scored into the book on momentum alone. Targets may drift up to meet the price, but that is the analyst community chasing, not new information. Nothing scheduled before the AGM and the H1 update well outside this horizon.
catalysts: Broker target revisions catching up to the price, or failing to
H1 FY27 trading update, outside this horizon
risks: Price roughly 20% above the A$139.20 average analyst target
FY26 underlying earnings fell 2%; US$7.1B impairments drove a statutory loss
FY27 guidance is flat revenue and only ~5% underlying profit growth
SMA50 not aligned: it qualified on momentum, not trend structure
invalidation: Flips long only on a pullback that holds - a close back above A$169 after testing the SMA50, with brokers actually raising targets to meet it. The bear case confirms on a close below A$155 native, which would give back most of the post-results gap.
